pages.text: Day 1 of the mathematics. Absolute Infinity is no longer a shortcut. To build it I have to build mathematics itself, one branch at a time.

The branches: $(thing)numbers$(), $(thing)analysis$(), $(thing)number theory$(), $(thing)topology$(), $(thing)logic$(), $(thing)sets$() and $(thing)categories$() - each with its own machine and its own symbols.

The $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$() builds number systems, the $(item)Analytic Continuator$() does calculus and analysis, the $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$() does logic, set theory and category theory, and the $(item)Cantor Diagonalizer$() takes it all to infinity.
Finally, whole stacks of every branch are compressed into a $(item)Mathematics Singularity$(), which - with Surreal Numbers, Toposes and Continuum Shards - becomes $(item)Absolute Infinity$().
One, two, three... Peano built all of arithmetic from zero and "the next one".$(br2)Made in $(item)Peano Arithmetic Engine$().
Real and imaginary at right angles. Every polynomial finally has its roots.$(br2)Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().
Larger than every infinity. It cannot be conceived - and yet here it is.$(br2)Made in $(item)Omnilex Engine$().

$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Natural Number Lattice$(): Aleph-Null Shard, Axiom Schema, Axiom Stone, Cantor Key, Empty Set and more$(li)$(item)Complex Plane$(): Empirical Notes II, Fourier Series, Fractal Set, Mathematics Singularity, Modular Form and more$(li)$(item)Absolute Infinity$(): Absolute Infinity, Absolute Notes III, Absolute Singularity, Arbor Simulacrum, Axiom Key and more
